aisBaselineNote: transitsBaseline is withheld (null) until 72 hourly samples exist on the current tiled12-active30m basis. The basis reset on 2026-07-30, when the AIS scraper stopped taking one thinned request for the whole bounding box and began tiling it so each tile is saturated, stepping counts up roughly 3.4x on total; the median is withheld again until enough post-cutover samples build up, the same as it was for roughly 3 days after the first cutover on 2026-07-20. Samples on an earlier basis are not mixed in. It is an AIS concurrent-presence median, a different population from transits.baseline (IMF PortWatch daily crossings); do not divide one by the other.

aisGaps.countScope: count is a floor on hulls we stopped receiving, not a count of evasions. Read it against eligibleTankers, the screened tanker population, and against ambientDarkRate, the share of eligible non-tankers that went dark on the identical test. The two rates are close, so the evasion excess is not currently distinguishable from ambient dropout.
aisGaps.vesselsTrackedScope: vesselsTracked is a cumulative, all-time, all-type total (every vessel ever recorded anywhere in the wider AIS bbox). It is not the screened population behind count: that population is tankers only, with 50 or more sightings, last seen inside the core area.

capeSnapshot.note: transitsLast24h counts port arrivals only (departures are not published upstream), across ports on both sides of the strait. Not a Hormuz crossing count. Use transits.count for that. An arrival is a port-area entry event rather than a distinct hull: adjacent ports double count and an anchorage reposition can re-trigger one, so read arrivals24hTotal as an activity index. expectedTotal is a 30-day forward book (ships expected within the next 30 days), not a queue waiting now.

chokepointsNote: preCrisisBaselineMedian on every row is computed over one fixed window (baselineWindowStart to baselineWindowEnd) anchored to the Hormuz crisis. For hormuz that window is a genuine pre-crisis baseline. For bab-el-mandeb, suez and cape it is not: those routes were already carrying diverted Red Sea traffic within that window, so preCrisisBaselineMedian for those rows reads as wartime volume, not a peacetime figure.

dailyBrief.summary: The Strait of Hormuz remains under severe operational stress. The IMF PortWatch figure for 2026-08-16, the most recent published day, recorded 1 transit against a pre-crisis baseline of 73 transits per day; PortWatch publishes weekly on Tuesdays and this figure carries a multi-day lag. Separately, port arrivals across the Hormuz-area ports on both the Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman sides reached 494 in the most recent 24 hours, a distinct methodology that does not map directly to the PortWatch transit count. As of 11:53 UTC, 201 hulls were holding position away from berth. The site's Crisis Pressure index sits in the extreme band, flat over the past 24 hours, with physical transit deviation as the top contributor; the Escalation Forecast index sits in the elevated band, also flat, driven by Polymarket escalation contracts. The two indices diverge, measuring state and trajectory separately. Brent stood at $91.70, up +0.84% over 24 hours, as of 11:53 UTC. On the incident front, Iranian state media carries a claim that Tehran warned Washington against seizing the strait; US and independent sources have not confirmed this. A cargo ship was declared a constructive total loss following multiple projectile strikes off Yemen, per gCaptain. Breitbart separately reports Chinese state shipping companies are pulling back from Hormuz chokepoints, though that report is unverified and single-source.

pipelineBypass.name: Petroline (East-West Pipeline)
pipelineBypass.notes: Saudi Aramco's East-West Pipeline carries Arabian Light from Abqaiq to Yanbu on the Red Sea, the single largest non-Hormuz route for Gulf crude.

pipelineBypass.name: ADCOP (Habshan-Fujairah)
pipelineBypass.notes: ADNOC's Habshan-Fujairah pipeline lifts UAE crude past the Strait of Hormuz to Fujairah on the Gulf of Oman, where it loads on tankers transiting the open Indian Ocean.

pipelineBypass.name: Goreh-Jask Pipeline
pipelineBypass.notes: Iran's pipeline from the southwest oilfields to Jask on the Gulf of Oman bypasses the Strait, but throughput remains a fraction of nameplate capacity.

premium.note: Machine-payable premium endpoints (x402, USDC on Base): full vessel manifest with sanctions cross-reference, single-vessel dossiers, a shadow-fleet risk screen of the vessels active on AIS in the Persian Gulf window, hourly history capped at one year with actual depth growing daily, bulk export, one-call snapshot, structured daily brief, real-time streaming, threshold-alert webhooks, and a Hormuz flag rollup. $0.01-$0.50 per request, no key or account. MCP connector at the mcp URL.

strandedNote: `stranded` counts every vessel not under way anywhere in the watch box, including ones at berth working cargo at regional ports such as Dubai and Abu Dhabi. `strandedOffshore` excludes vessels within 25km of a working port and is the narrower figure the site's own narrative uses.

transits.cadenceNote: Completed daily transits (IMF PortWatch crossing count). Not the same as aisConcurrentInZone, which is a snapshot of vessels moving inside the wider Persian Gulf watch box right now, not the Strait channel itself.
transits.freshestDayNote: The newest PortWatch row is always a Sunday, because IMF publishes weekly on Tuesday against data carrying a ~2-day lag. Sunday is the lowest-traffic weekday in this series, so the freshest print reads low against the day before it even in a normal week. Compare it with earlier Sundays, or with baselineMedian, rather than with previousNTotal.

verdict.long: War-risk insurance has priced commercial transit through the Strait of Hormuz beyond the reach of most operators.
